title: The star cluster NGC 6604 and its surroundings
caption: The star cluster NGC 6604 and the nebula Sh2-54, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope at La Silla
celestial: NGC 6604 · constellation Serpens Cauda · about 5500 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: A bright grouping of stars toward the upper left of this image is the young star cluster NGC 6604. Around it lie the cluster's associated nebula, a cloud of glowing hydrogen gas called Sh2-54, and clouds of dust. The picture was taken by the Wide Field Imager on the 2.2-meter MPG/ESO telescope at ESO's La Silla Observatory in Chile.

The cluster forms the densest part of a looser association of about one hundred brilliant blue-white stars. A stellar association is a widely spread group of young stars that share a common origin but are only weakly held together by gravity, if at all.

Clouds of glowing hydrogen like Sh2-54 typically shine because ultraviolet light from hot young stars makes the gas glow. NGC 6604 and its surroundings mark a region where stars have recently formed and some of the raw material still remains.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (34.31 x 33.26 arcminutes) and distance (5500 light years), the frame spans roughly 55 × 53 light-years. Its light set out about 5,500 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image from the Wide Field Imager combines U, B, V, R and hydrogen-alpha filters, from the ultraviolet end of the spectrum through visible light. The color assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: Long exposures and a hydrogen-alpha filter bring out faint glowing gas that the eye could not see directly.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.

explore: NGC 6604 lies about 5,500 light-years away in the direction of Serpens Cauda. The image combines five filters spanning ultraviolet and visible light, including one that isolates the red glow of hydrogen.
alt: A bright group of stars at upper left amid a cloud of glowing hydrogen gas and dust clouds.
